title: Field quantization in rotating frames: coordinate covariance and the circular-detector response
authors: Sidney Natzuka Junior, Carlos Augusto Domingues Zarro, Matheus dos Santos Soares
abstract: We provide a unified analysis of scalar-field quantization and detector response in relativistic rotating frames, comparing rigid and Trocheris-Takeno (TT) descriptions in unbounded Minkowski spacetime. We distinguish three questions that are often conflated: (i) how a fixed quantum state is represented in rotating coordinates, (ii) whether rotating time evolution selects a global ground state, and (iii) how a rotating detector responds to the vacuum. Coordinate-transformed rigid and TT modes span the same positive-frequency subspace as inertial modes: their Bogoliubov beta coefficients vanish and their mode sums reproduce the Minkowski Wightman function. Neither rotating time flow selects a global scalar ground state, although for different reasons: the rigid generator is not globally timelike and is unbounded below, whereas TT time translation is not a Killing symmetry. Nevertheless, a circular Unruh-DeWitt detector in the Minkowski vacuum has a stationary, nonzero response. We relate this response to negative corotating frequencies, evaluate it after an explicit Hadamard subtraction, and show that it is nonthermal. Thus vanishing Bogoliubov mixing, the absence of a symmetry-selected rotating vacuum, and detector excitation are mutually consistent.
summary: This theoretical paper rigorously analyzes quantum field quantization in rotating frames, comparing different mathematical descriptions (rigid vs. TT). It resolves the apparent conflict between the lack of a symmetry-selected vacuum state and the detection of a non-zero, non-thermal signal from a detector in the vacuum. The findings establish a consistent framework for understanding vacuum fluctuations in non-inertial settings.
main_problem: The paper provides a unified analysis of scalar-field quantization and detector response in relativistic rotating frames, comparing rigid and Trocheris-Takeno (TT) descriptions in Minkowski spacetime.
main_result: The authors show that while neither rotating time flow selects a global ground state, a circular Unruh-DeWitt detector in the Minkowski vacuum exhibits a stationary, non-thermal response, demonstrating the mutual consistency of these seemingly disparate effects.
method: The analysis employs mode decomposition using Bogoliubov coefficients, compares different coordinate representations (rigid vs. TT), and calculates the detector response using Hadamard subtraction.
model_or_system: The system involves a real scalar field quantized in the Minkowski vacuum, coupled to a two-level Unruh-DeWitt detector, analyzed under the influence of rotating coordinates.
key_observables: Bogoliubov beta coefficients, detector excitation rate spectrum, Minkowski Wightman function, and the non-thermal nature of the detector response.
important_parameters: The analysis is performed in the context of Minkowski spacetime, focusing on the comparison between inertial, rigid, and TT modes.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the Minkowski vacuum and makes a crucial distinction between the state definition, time evolution selection, and detector response.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing quantization requirements, comparing rigid and TT transformations, demonstrating the failure of these flows to select a global ground state, confirming the mode equivalence via vanishing Bogoliubov coefficients, and finally calculating the non-thermal detector response.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the subtleties of defining vacuum states and thermalization in non-inertial frames, which is critical for understanding quantum field theory in curved or accelerating backgrounds relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems.
